answer: Rotating rendezvous assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws one pearl slot per identity from a large space; only holders of that epoch's slot may act, and slots reshuffle before attackers learn them. Since slots are unpredictable, an attacker must pre-commit agents to every possible slot, paying full per-agent cost: collateral, jade bond upkeep, and ivory audit fees each epoch. Dupes then cost nearly the same as honest seats, so mass registration yields no discount or edge.
